business_summary: NIKE designs, markets and sells athletic footwear, apparel and equipment under the NIKE, Jordan and Converse brands. It contracts out almost all manufacturing and earns the gap between what product costs to make and what the brand lets it charge. FY2026 (year ended 31 May 2026) revenue was $46.4B. In Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 31 Aug 2026) revenue was $11,213M, down 4% (-5% currency-neutral): North America $5,127M (+2%), EMEA $3,176M (-5%), Greater China $1,180M (-22%, -26% currency-neutral), APLA $1,463M (-2%), Converse $263M (-28%). By channel, Wholesale $6,804M (-1%) and NIKE Direct $4,142M (-8%; digital -13%, owned stores -5%). The business reset under CEO Elliott Hill (returned October 2024) has moved from 'pull back from discounted digital, rebuild wholesale' to a broader restructuring: on 1 Oct 2026 NIKE announced the 'Pace' program (about $1.0B of pre-tax charges through FY2031 for about $2.5B of cumulative savings), a consolidation from four geographic regions to three, and guided FY2027 revenue to decline high-single digits with adjusted EPS of only $1.15-$1.35. The thesis question is unchanged but sharper: can a still-dominant brand stop shrinking in China, digital and lifestyle (Sportswear, Jordan, Converse) before the brand premium itself erodes? Performance/running is the one clear bright spot.

moat.type: Brand / intangible assets, scale in sports marketing and athlete endorsement, global distribution and sourcing scale
moat.rationale: Kept at NARROW. Evidence the brand moat still exists: Q1 FY2027 gross margin rose 60bps to 42.8% even with revenue down 4%, the FY2026 gross margin was 42.9% and FY2026 ROIC about 22% (our calculation), and running grew double digits in Q1 with NIKE Performance up high-single digits — NIKE can still win a category when it puts product behind it. Evidence it is being worn down: Greater China fell 22% in Q1 (a ninth consecutive quarterly decline, our count from the eight reported through Q4 FY2026), and the 10-Q says China challenges are expected to extend beyond fiscal 2027; NIKE Digital fell 13%; Jordan fell mid-teens; Sportswear fell low double digits with Dunk down nearly 50%; Converse fell 28%. Lifestyle franchises are where brand heat shows, and they are shrinking. We do not downgrade to 'none' because pricing power (gross margin) is holding; we would downgrade if gross margin breaks below 40%.

valuation.method: pe + fcf_yield (equal-weighted average of the two bands, computed by code/valuation.py)
valuation.method_detail: P/E leg: midpoint of management's FY2027 ADJUSTED diluted EPS guidance, $1.25 (range $1.15-$1.35, excluding about $0.15 of Pace restructuring charges), x 15 / 20 / 25 = $18.75 / $25.00 / $31.25. We switched the anchor from trailing GAAP EPS ($2.10 for FY2026, which included a one-time $0.52 IEEPA tariff-recovery benefit) to forward guidance because the company has now told us FY2027 earnings will be roughly 40% lower than the clean FY2026 base (~$1.58). We use HIGHER multiples than last time (13/17/21x) because $1.25 is plausibly a trough year depressed by restructuring, tariffs and China; 15x = earnings stay near this level (a no-growth, shrinking brand), 20x = gradual recovery, 25x = the Pace savings ($2.5B cumulative through FY2031) and a performance-led turnaround work and the market pays a recovery multiple on trough earnings. FCF-yield leg: trailing-twelve-month free cash flow $2,105M / 1,484.2M diluted shares = $1.418 per share, at required yields of 6.0% / 5.0% / 4.0% = $23.63 / $28.36 / $35.45. We keep the demanding yields because FCF has fallen for two straight years, was negative in Q1 FY2027 and does not cover the dividend.
valuation.margin_of_safety_definition: (base fair value - price) / base fair value, as returned by code/valuation.py
valuation.verdict: expensive — the price ($34.25) is above even the HIGH end of our fair-value band ($33.35). NOT a buy.
valuation.caveats: (1) The P/E leg rests on company GUIDANCE, not reported results; guidance has already been cut once (Reuters-reported analyst consensus before the print was about a 2% FY2027 revenue decline vs the guided high-single-digit decline). (2) The FCF leg uses trailing cash flow that includes FY2026 strength and does not yet reflect the guided earnings drop; if FY2027 FCF falls in line with earnings, this leg is too generous. (3) The ~$986M IEEPA tariff recovery booked in Q4 FY2026 has not been confirmed as collected in cash: neither the Q1 release nor the 10-Q (per our review of a third-party rendering) nor the call addressed it — status unknown. A cash collection would be a one-time ~$0.66/share inflow that we have NOT added to the band. (4) We may miss a recovery; a missed buy costs nothing.

conviction_note: Lowered from 2 to 1 (avoid for now). Reasons: (a) management guided FY2027 revenue down high-single digits, which effectively pre-announces our 'third year of revenue decline' sell trigger; (b) the 10-Q says Greater China challenges extend beyond FY2027 and the CFO said China 'gets worse' for the rest of the year, which meets the spirit of our China trigger; (c) Q1 free cash flow was negative and the dividend is uncovered for a second year on any reasonable FY2027 path; (d) the price is above the high end of our fair-value band. Offsetting: the balance sheet is still net cash, gross margin rose, and running is growing double digits. Conviction 1 is not 'never' — we would revisit at a price in the low $20s AND with evidence that China and Sportswear have stopped falling.
summary: Q1 FY2027 (quarter to 31 Aug 2026) made the NIKE turnaround look longer and more expensive, not closer. Revenue fell 4% to $11.2B, Greater China fell 22%, NIKE Digital fell 13%, Converse fell 28%, and management guided full-year revenue down high-single digits with adjusted EPS of $1.15-$1.35 — roughly 40% below the clean FY2026 base — while launching a $1.0B 'Pace' restructuring and a regional reorganisation. The good news is real but narrow: gross margin rose 60bps to 42.8%, operating overhead fell 6%, running grew double digits, North America grew 2%, and the balance sheet still holds about $475M of net cash. On filing-backed numbers our fair-value band is $21.19 / $26.68 / $33.35, and the stock at $34.25 is above the top of it, implying the market is already paying for a recovery. Verdict: AVOID for now (conviction 1). We do not own it, so no sell action is needed; several of our pre-written thesis-break triggers are now guided to be hit in FY2027.
bull_case: Pricing power is holding even in a bad year: Q1 FY2027 gross margin rose 60bps to 42.8% on lower warehousing and logistics costs, despite revenue falling 4%.

The performance turnaround is visible: NIKE Performance grew high-single digits and Running grew double digits in Q1 FY2027, and North America grew 2% with management citing strong sell-through at sporting-goods retailers. That is where 'Win Now' started, and it is working.

Costs are coming down: operating overhead fell 6% to $2,658M in Q1, and the Pace program targets about $2.5B of cumulative savings through FY2031 for about $1.0B of charges, with maximum savings around FY2029-FY2030.

The balance sheet still cannot force a bad decision: $8,368M of cash and short-term investments vs $7,893M of total debt (net cash about $475M, -0.10x EBITDA). There is no buyback cash drain (repurchases were $0 in Q1).

Management is explicit that the dividend is protected: the CFO said 'under all scenarios, we have support for maintaining and ultimately growing the dividend over time,' and the quarterly dividend was raised to $0.41 from $0.40.
A possible one-time cash inflow: the ~$986M IEEPA tariff recovery booked in Q4 FY2026, if collected (status unknown), is about $0.66 per share.

Sentiment is washed out — removal from the S&P 100, a twelve-year low, multiple downgrades, and a guidance cut — so expectations are low. A new board member from LVMH (Alexandre Arnault, effective 16 Sep 2026) adds luxury-brand experience to the board.
risks: China is getting worse, not stabilising. Q1 FY2027 Greater China revenue fell 22% (-26% currency-neutral) to $1,180M and China EBIT fell to $248M from $377M. The 10-Q cites declining store traffic, elevated promotion and high inventory, and says the challenges are expected to extend beyond fiscal 2027; the CFO said China 'actually gets worse from a revenue perspective for the balance of this year.' Trailing-twelve-month China revenue is now about $5.47B (our estimate from FY2026's rounded $5.8B), approaching our $5.0B trigger.

Guided earnings collapse. FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.15-$1.35 compares with FY2026 GAAP EPS of $2.10 (about $1.58 excluding the one-time tariff recovery). At $34.25 the stock trades at roughly 27x the guidance midpoint — not cheap for a business guiding revenue down high-single digits.

Lifestyle brand heat is fading: Jordan (about 13% of the business) fell mid-teens, Sportswear fell low double digits, the Dunk franchise fell nearly 50% (about a $200M headwind), and Converse fell 28%. These are the franchises that made NIKE culturally dominant.

Cash flow does not cover the dividend. Q1 FY2027 free cash flow was -$64M ($135M CFO - $199M capex) against $610M of dividends; FY2026 FCF of $2,184M was already below $2,407M of dividends. With FY2027 earnings guided sharply lower, a second year of uncovered dividends looks likely, funded from the shrinking net-cash cushion.

Restructuring execution risk: Pace is a five-year program ($1.0B of charges through FY2031) layered on a two-year-old turnaround, plus a cut from four to three regions. Restructurings during a sales decline can damage the product engine and culture they are meant to fix.
Structural share loss in running/lifestyle to On, HOKA, New Balance and adidas (third-party data from the prior thesis); NIKE's running rebound is from a low base.
Inventory rose 5% from 31 May 2026 to $7,846M while revenue fell, attributed to product mix — worth watching against our 'inventory faster than revenue' red-flag trigger.
Tariffs remain a cost and pricing headwind; the status of the IEEPA refund is unknown.
Valuation risk the other way: if the turnaround works, our band will miss part of the recovery. We accept that.
what_would_break_thesis: Gross margin (excluding one-time tariff recoveries) falls below 40.0% for two consecutive quarters. Q1 FY2027: 42.8%; FY2026: 42.91%.

FY2027 total revenue comes in below FY2026's $46,398M — STATUS: management guided a high-single-digit decline on 2026-10-01, so this is expected to be hit. (Original wording: a third consecutive fiscal year below the FY2024 $51,362M peak.)

Trailing-twelve-month Greater China revenue below $5.0B, or China declines continuing past the end of FY2027 — STATUS: TTM is about $5.47B (estimate) and the 10-Q says challenges are expected to extend beyond fiscal 2027, so the second half of this trigger is effectively confirmed by management.
Free cash flow below $1.5B in a fiscal year, or below dividends paid for a second consecutive year (FY2026 FCF $2,184M vs dividends $2,407M) — STATUS: at risk; Q1 FY2027 FCF -$64M vs dividends $610M.
Net debt to EBITDA above 1.5x (currently -0.10x, net cash of about $475M), or total debt rising while free cash flow falls.
A dividend cut (management says it will maintain and grow it 'under all scenarios').

Full-year EBIT margin below 7.0% (FY2026 8.3%; Q1 FY2027 8.1%). With guided adjusted EPS of $1.15-$1.35 on revenue down high-single digits, FY2027 EBIT margin is likely to fall well below 7% (our inference from guidance) — treat as expected to be hit.
NIKE Direct still declining into FY2028 with wholesale growth below 2% (Q1 FY2027: Direct -8%, wholesale -1%).
Departure of CEO Elliott Hill, or a further major strategy reset beyond the October 2026 Pace program and regional consolidation, before FY2028.

Any accounting red flag: restatement, material weakness, disputed auditor change, or inventory growing much faster than revenue for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY2027: inventory +5% vs 31 May while revenue fell 4% y/y — one quarter, watch).
sell_triggers: Gross margin (ex one-time tariff recoveries) below 40.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY2027: 42.8%).
FY2027 revenue below FY2026's $46,398M (guided to be hit).
TTM Greater China revenue below $5.0B (now ~ $5.47B est.), or China declines beyond FY2027 (management says challenges extend beyond FY2027).
Free cash flow below $1.5B in a fiscal year, or below dividends for a second consecutive year.
Full-year EBIT margin below 7.0% (FY2026 8.3%; likely to be hit in FY2027 per guidance).
NIKE Direct still declining into FY2028 with wholesale growth below 2%.
Departure of CEO Elliott Hill or a further major strategy reset before FY2028.
Any accounting red flag: restatement, material weakness, disputed auditor change, or inventory growing much faster than revenue for two consecutive quarters.
Because we do NOT own NKE, these triggers currently function as 'do not buy' gates: any new BUY requires that the guided-to-be-hit triggers are explicitly re-underwritten in a refreshed thesis.
catalysts: Q2 FY2027 results (quarter ending 30 Nov 2026), expected late December 2026 (date unknown). Management flagged about 400bps of revenue headwind in Q2 from prior-year comparisons (EMEA Cyber Week promotions and North America sell-in).
China marketplace reset: management says China revenue worsens for the rest of FY2027; watch whether the decline rate peaks.
Pace program execution: size and timing of the ~$0.3B FY2027 charge and evidence of overhead savings.
Collection (or not) of the ~$986M IEEPA tariff recovery receivable — status unknown.
Regional consolidation to three regions (Americas; Asia Pacific and Greater China; EMEA) — will change segment reporting, so our China trigger may need re-basing once new segments are reported.
FY2028 outlook (likely with Q4 FY2027 results around late June 2027) — the first test of whether FY2027 is the trough.

sources.claim: NIKE shares closed at a twelve-year low of $39.09 on 1 September 2026, about 78% below their November 2021 peak, after an eighth straight quarter of declining China sales. JPMorgan downgraded NIKE to Underweight, citing a China online-marketplace reset beginning January 2027 that it estimates as an unmitigated revenue headwind of more than $1B a year (about 20% of the region's revenue), rising tariff costs pressuring earnings through fiscal 2028, and continued share loss to HOKA and On in North America.
sources.value: JPMorgan Underweight; China marketplace reset from January 2027 estimated at >$1B annual revenue headwind

data_quality_note: Revenue, margins, EBIT, EPS, balance sheet, cash flow, dividends, buybacks, guidance and restructuring figures come from NIKE's Q1 FY2027 8-K (Exhibit 99.1 and Item 2.05), the Q1 FY2027 10-Q XBRL, and the FY2026 8-K/10-K on SEC EDGAR. Price and moving averages come from Alpaca. ESTIMATED / NON-REPORTED items, clearly labelled: (1) the P/E anchor is company GUIDANCE ($1.15-$1.35 adjusted EPS), not a reported result; (2) TTM Greater China revenue (~$5.47B) uses FY2026's rounded $5.8B; (3) net-debt/EBITDA uses FY2026 EBITDA as the trailing proxy; (4) ROIC is our own calculation (FY2026, excludes leases); (5) some 10-Q narrative (China 'beyond fiscal 2027', inventory +5%, dividends paid $610M) was read via a third-party rendering of the filing, not the EDGAR HTML directly; (6) call commentary comes from a transcript published by The Motley Fool; (7) the IEEPA refund status is unknown. Sensitivity cases contain explicit analyst assumptions and are not used for the headline band.
